interest: Japanese cultural and nationalist societies of the 1930s.
overview: This file consists of six State Department 'List of Papers' docket registry sheets for decimal file 894.43 (internal affairs of Japan: societies) spanning 1932 to 1938. The sheets catalogue incoming and outgoing despatches, letters, and cross-reference entries tracking a wide variety of Japanese political, cultural, bilateral, and nationalist organizations. Key subjects indexed include reactionary youth training organizations and Kenzo Adachi's Kokumin Domei; the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinko Kai) headed by Prince Fumimaro Konoe, detailing its founding, publications, and establishment of a New York branch; the America-Japan Society and its activities in Tokyo and Wakayama; an inquiry from the Boy Scouts of America regarding the International Goodwill Koi-nobori Society; the formation of the Philippine-Japan Society; and an open letter from the reactionary Shiunso society regarding Japan's policy toward China and Manchuria.
